title: D365 Architect table definition
description: Declarative YAML shape for a Dynamics table, produced by `d365architect table export`. A field left out of this file was left at Dataverse's own default, not "unknown" — see each field's own description for what that default is. Editing this file back into Dataverse (via the matching `import` command) will leave an omitted field at that default rather than whatever it happened to be before.

entity.description: The table's logical name, e.g. "account" — written as the top-level "entity" key.

schemaName.description: The customization-prefixed schema name, e.g. "new_BankAccount". Fixed at creation time — required when creating a table, immutable after.

displayName.description: The table's singular display name, e.g. "Account".

pluralDisplayName.description: The table's plural display name, e.g. "Accounts".

ownershipType.description: "UserOwned", "OrganizationOwned", etc. Required to create a table; can't be changed afterwards.

isActivity.description: Only present when true — false is the platform default for a table. Omit to leave it as an ordinary table; applying this file back won't make it an activity type.

hasActivities.description: Only present when true — false is the platform default for a table. Omit to leave activities off for this table; applying this file back won't turn them on.

hasNotes.description: Only present when true — false is the platform default for a table. Omit to leave notes off for this table; applying this file back won't turn them on.

schemaName.description: The customization-prefixed schema name, e.g. "new_BankName". Required to create a column; immutable after.

physicalName.description: The underlying SQL column name, when it differs from the logical name in more than casing — only present when exported from a legacy unpacked solution's Entity.xml; live exports never set this, since Dataverse manages its own storage rather than mapping columns onto SQL Server directly.

requiredLevel.description: "recommended", "applicationrequired" or "systemrequired". Only present when set to something other than "none" — that's Dataverse's default for every column type. Omit for an optional column; applying this file back won't add a requirement level.

precision.description: Decimal places. For Money, only meaningful when precisionSource is 2 (this column's own).

precisionSource.description: Money only: 0 = currency-specific, 1 = organization setting, 2 = this column's own precision.

targets.description: Lookup/Customer/Owner: logical names of the table(s) this column can point to.

isCustomField.description: Only present when true — false (a standard, non-custom field) is by far the common case. Purely informational: applying this file back never changes it either way — whether a column is custom is determined by how it was created, not something re-set on update.

validForAdvancedFind.description: Whether this column can be used in Advanced Find.

options.description: A Picklist/MultiSelectPicklist/State/Status column's own choice values, when it's backed by a *local* option set — null instead when it's backed by a global one (see GlobalOptionSetName; confirmed live that State/Status in particular normally are). Never set together with GlobalOptionSetName — a column uses one or the other, never both. See AttributeOptionDefinition for why Value is always explicit.

value.description: The option's integer value, e.g. 727000000. Ignored for a Status option being newly inserted — see this class's own doc comment.

state.description: Status only: which State (0 = Active, 1 = Inactive, by Dataverse's own convention — a table can define more) this status reason belongs to. Required to insert a brand-new Status option — Dataverse's InsertStatusValue action needs it and this tool never guesses it — but not otherwise meaningful (Picklist/ MultiSelectPicklist/State options don't have one; a State option's own Value already is its state).

globalOptionSetName.description: The shared GlobalOptionSetDefinitions choice this column uses instead of its own local Options — applies to Picklist/MultiSelectPicklist, and, confirmed live, State/Status too (every statecode/statuscode checked on a real tenant, standard and custom tables alike, turned out to be backed by a global {entity}_statecode/{entity}_statuscode choice, not a local one). This tool only ever *references* an existing global choice by name — it never creates, edits, or deletes one, since that's a shared, cross-table resource with a much wider blast radius than a single column; this also means State/Status option-renaming is inert whenever this is set (see `docs/yaml-conventions.md`).

defaultValue.description: Boolean only: the value a new record gets for this column when nothing else is set.

trueOptionLabel.description: Boolean only: the label shown for "true". Omitted when it's Dataverse's own default, "True".

falseOptionLabel.description: Boolean only: the label shown for "false". Omitted when it's Dataverse's own default, "False".

relationshipSchemaName.description: Lookup only, required to create a brand-new Lookup column: the schema name of the one-to-many relationship that owns this lookup — a separate name from the column's own SchemaName, never inferred. Not used for Customer (its two relationship names are derived from SchemaName instead — see `docs/yaml-conventions.md`) or for any other type.

relationshipBehavior.description: Lookup only: the new relationship's Behavior — "Referential", "ReferentialRestrictDelete", or "Parental" (see RelationshipBehaviors). Only present when set to something other than "Referential" — the Maker UI's own default for a brand-new lookup, and the only one of the three that never collides with another Parental relationship the referencing table might already have (see `docs/yaml-conventions.md`).
